root_cause.text: The Linux kernel lacks a notification mechanism to inform the IOMMU when kernel page table pages are freed, allowing the IOMMU to cache stale entries for kernel virtual addresses when Shared Virtual Addressing (SVA) is enabled on x86, leading to use-after-free or write-after-free conditions.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states, "The Linux kernel currently lacks a notification mechanism for kernel page table changes, specifically when page table pages are freed and reused. The IOMMU driver is only notified of changes to user virtual address mappings. This can cause the IOMMU's internal caches to retain stale entries for kernel VA." The patch disables SVA on x86 (adding `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_X86)) return ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP);`) because the x86 architecture maps kernel virtual address space into every process's page table, enabling the IOMMU to walk and cache kernel page table entries.
